We exercise, eat healthy food, and seek medical attention when we feel unwell. However, one aspect of health that is equally important—but often overlooked—is our mental health and emotional wellbeing. The way we think, feel, and cope with life's challenges significantly impacts our overall quality of life. With increasing stress, anxiety, relationship challenges, work pressure, financial concerns, and social expectations, mental health has become more important than ever before. Understanding Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing Mental health refers to our emotional, psychological, and social wellbeing. It influences how we think, feel, behave, and interact with others. Emotional wellbeing, on the other hand, reflects our ability to manage emotions, cope with stress, build healthy relationships, and maintain a positive outlook on life. Good mental health does not mean feeling happy all the time. It means having the resilience and coping skills needed to navigate life's ups and downs while maintaining balance and self-awareness. The mind-body connection refers to the relationship between our mental and emotional states and our physical health. Our thoughts, feelings, beliefs, and attitudes can positively or negatively affect biological functioning. Do you feel like you've lost a part of yourself while trying to keep someone else happy? If so, you may have experienced narcissistic abuse. Unlike physical abuse, narcissistic abuse often leaves invisible wounds. It can deeply affect a person's confidence, emotional wellbeing, relationships, and sense of identity. The good news is that recovery is possible. With awareness, support, and healing, you can rebuild your life and rediscover your authentic self. What Is Narcissistic Abuse? Narcissistic abuse is a pattern of emotional, psychological, and sometimes financial or social manipulation used by individuals who display strong narcissistic traits or behaviors. These individuals often seek control, validation, admiration, and power over others. While they may initially appear charming, caring, and attentive, the relationship gradually becomes emotionally draining and confusing.
